requirement: OPS-05: verifiable device sparse forward/backward, update/restore and measurement
scope: Hardware Apple M3 Metal float32 sparse drive and local derivative, plus a scalar zero-delay dynamics adapter that uses those GPU primitives at every recurrent step. This does not meet the full OPS-05 device training contract.

environment.machine: Mac15,12 Apple M3, 16 GiB unified memory

observed_result.gpu_tests: PASS; no hardware tests skipped on this Mac
observed_result.cpu_reference: 130 nodes, 910 edges; per-edge and source gradients all matched independent float32 CPU reference, max absolute difference 0 with test tolerance 1e-6
observed_result.regression: The prior source-row loop intermittently left weight-gradient slots unwritten; a separate GPU invocation per CSR edge slot plus sentinel-buffer test passed full package 20 repetitions and 130-node test 100 repetitions.
observed_result.dynamics_adapter: GPUContinuous scalar zero-delay forward/backward with four recurrent steps and truncated BPTT matched float64 CPU within declared 4e-5 absolute and relative tolerance; both test and race runs had no skips.
observed_result.no_silent_cpu_fallback: Forward-only adapter Backward returns ErrGPUContinuousBackwardUnavailable; construction with backward checks a fixed GPU result before exposing the adapter.

limitations: This is a float32 GPU sparse primitive and a host-orchestrated float64 scalar zero-delay adapter, not an optimizer or device-resident training loop.
The host still computes activation, time constants and state update; weights, inputs and gradients transfer each step, and the CPU restores declared edge order from CSR.
Device-side parameter update, trainer integration, capacity checks for a full graph, state save/restore and Ubuntu RTX4070 or Windows execution remain unverified.
Phase times are single host observations around API calls, not GPU timestamp queries or a measured speedup.
The failed shader path was isolated to storage writes in a source-row loop; the underlying Metal/WGSL compiler layer causing the omission is not proven.
